subject: general
question: After brazing, hammering the joint serves to _________.

options.text: check for leakages and remove flux

solution:
The correct answer is __check for leakages and remove flux.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hammering the joint after brazing__ is typically done to check for leakages and remove flux from the joint.
 
• This process ensures that the joint is free of defects and maintains its integrity.
 
• Flux removal is essential to prevent corrosion and enhance the durability of the joint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Brazing:**

 
 
• Brazing is a metal-joining process in which a filler metal is heated above its melting point and distributed between two or more close-fitting parts by capillary action.
 
• It is used to join different types of metals and produces a strong, sealed joint.
 
 
 
• **Flux:**
 
 
• Flux is a chemical agent used in brazing to clean and protect the metal surfaces from oxidation during the process.
 
• Proper removal of flux after brazing is important to prevent corrosion and ensure joint strength.
